hero_kpi_rationale: Aviva reports a 25% increase in operating profit reaching £2.2 billion, reflecting strong performance across all segments (insurance, asset management, health).

kpis.name: Adjusted Operating Profit
kpis.explanation: Core adjusted earnings of the company, excluding exceptional items.
kpis.description: Aviva reports a 25% increase in operating profit in 2025, driven by improved performance in general insurance, wealth management, and health.

kpis.name: Operating Earnings Per Share
kpis.explanation: Operating profit divided by the number of shares outstanding.
kpis.description: Operating EPS reaches 56.0 pence in 2025, up 17%, supported by earnings growth and effective capital management.

kpis.name: Return on Equity (IFRS)
kpis.explanation: Return on equity under IFRS accounting standards.
kpis.description: IFRS RoE stands at 17.5% in 2025, up 1.8 percentage points, reflecting more efficient capital management and strong profit generation.

kpis.name: Operational Free Surplus Generation (Solvency II)
kpis.explanation: Operational free surplus generation under Solvency II framework.
kpis.description: Operational free surplus generation reaches £2.3 billion, up 40%, supported by robust performance in insurance and asset management businesses.

kpis.name: Cash Remittances
kpis.explanation: Cash flows remitted from subsidiaries to the holding company to fund dividends and share buybacks.
kpis.description: Cash remittances reach £2.1 billion in 2025, up 4%, confirming the group's ability to return capital to shareholders via dividends and buybacks.

kpis.name: General Insurance Premiums
kpis.explanation: Gross premiums written in property and casualty insurance.
kpis.description: General insurance premiums grow 18% at constant exchange rates in 2025, driven by the acquisition of Direct Line and organic growth.

kpis.name: General Insurance Combined Ratio
kpis.explanation: Technical combined ratio measuring operational efficiency in property and casualty insurance (claims + expenses / premiums).
kpis.description: The non-upwardly revised general insurance combined ratio stands at 94.6% in 2025, maintaining solid technical profitability despite the integration of Direct Line.

kpis.name: Wealth Assets Under Management
kpis.explanation: Total assets managed in wealth and investment management activities.
kpis.description: Wealth AUM reaches £234 billion at end-2025, supported by positive net flows of £10.9 billion.

kpis.name: Wealth Net Flows
kpis.explanation: Net subscriptions minus redemptions in wealth management activities.
kpis.description: Wealth net flows amount to £10.9 billion in 2025, representing 6% of opening AUM, reflecting strong commercial momentum.

kpis.name: Global Customers
kpis.description: Aviva serves 25.2 million customers globally at end-2025, up 4.7 million, driven in part by the acquisition of Direct Line.

kpis.name: UK Multi-product Customers
kpis.explanation: Number of UK customers holding at least two Aviva policies.
kpis.description: 7.2 million UK customers now hold at least two Aviva policies, up 1.8 million, illustrating the success of the cross-selling strategy.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 26.2 GBp in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of £1.246 billion in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last three fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Proportion of net income distributed as dividends: 120.6% in the latest year.

risks.title: Intensification of competition in UK and Canada markets
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly named in the filing ("increased competition in the UK and in other countries where we have significant operations"). Direct and unqualified language. Upward trend due to the acquisition of Direct Line and industry consolidation. Structurally important category for the UK's #1 general insurer.

risks.title: Regulatory risks related to Solvency UK and FCA Consumer Duty
risks.score_rationale: Highlighted as a priority in the filing with specific examples ("FCA Consumer Duty and Solvency UK", PRA internal model approval). Strong language ("regulatory approval", "changes to"). Upward trend with final PRA rules effective December 31, 2024. Critical category for solvency and product distribution.

risks.title: Cyberattacks and large-scale customer data theft
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly detailed in the filing ("cyber attacks, phishing/vishing attacks, theft, loss or misuse of customer data"). Specific and illustrated language. Stable to upward trend given a 25 million customer base and accelerated digital transformation. High weight for a group managing £234 billion in AUM.

risks.title: Dependence on third-party distribution channels and partners
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly named risk ("reliance on third-party distribution channels", "arrangements with third parties, including joint ventures"). Moderate but recurring language. Stable trend. Significant weight as ~40% of GI premiums come from non-retail channels according to the presentation.

risks.title: Risks related to the integration of Direct Line and future acquisitions
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned ("uncertainties relating to announced and future acquisitions", "diversion of management attention", "inability to integrate and deliver expected benefits"). Strong prudential language. New/up trend with the completion of the Direct Line acquisition on July 1, 2025. High weight: Direct Line represents ~£2.3 billion in share issuance.

risks.title: Exposure to Lloyd's risks through the acquisition of Probitas
risks.score_rationale: Highly specific and detailed risk in the filing ("dependence on Lloyd's credit rating, solvency position, maintenance of Lloyd's own licence"). Precise and technical language. New trend following the acquisition of Probitas. Moderate but growing weight with expansion into the GCS segment.

risks.title: Adoption of AI and technology risks related to new technologies
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly named risk ("adoption of and reliance on new and rapidly advancing technologies, such as artificial intelligence and quantum computing"). Forward-looking language with increasing intensity given the stated AI-first strategy. Upward trend with ~550 data scientists and active AI deployment in pricing, claims, and advisory.

risks.title: Reputational damage and loss of customer trust
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly named risk ("changes to our brand and reputation", "failure to act in good faith, resulting in customers not achieving good outcomes"). Direct language linked to Consumer Duty. Stable trend but sensitive in a context of consolidation (Direct Line) and digital transformation. Significant weight for a group with 25 million customers.

ai_positioning.summary: Aviva integrates artificial intelligence as a lever for operational transformation, particularly to improve efficiency and customer experience. It explicitly mentions the use of AI in its growth strategy.
evidence: "Unlocking Aviva's full potential – capital-light growth in General Insurance and Wealth, transforming with AI"
"the risks associated with adoption of and reliance on new and rapidly advancing technologies, such as artificial intelligence and quantum computing"
